# Qualification matrix

What this milestone claims, and what enforces each claim. Every name below is
resolved against the tree by `just qualification-matrix`, so a test that is
renamed or deleted turns that gate red instead of leaving this table asserting
something that is no longer checked.

## Enforced

| claim | enforced by |
|---|---|
| Every registration class the ABI exposes is served by the process boundary, and the set is pinned rather than counted. | Rust test `the_boundary_serves_a_named_subset_of_the_registration_surface` — `crates/plugin-host/tests/architecture.rs` |
| Only the shared composition starts a host, installs a proxy or loads a native plugin: a consumer cannot grow its own lifecycle semantics. | Rust test `only_the_composition_owner_assembles_the_process_boundary` — `crates/plugin-host/tests/architecture.rs`<br>Rust test `no_new_native_loading_appears_outside_the_grandfathered_paths` — `crates/plugin-host/tests/architecture.rs` |
| The kernel does not depend on the loader's implementation, and the dynamic loader is a dependency of one crate. | Rust test `the_loader_is_a_dependency_of_one_crate_and_the_kernel_does_not_depend_on_the_implementation` — `crates/plugin-host/tests/architecture.rs` |
| A registration reached across the boundary inherits the managed action's budget; no plugin-execution path invents one. | Rust test `no_plugin_execution_path_chooses_its_own_budget` — `crates/plugin-host/tests/architecture.rs` |
| A native plugin's library is loaded in the host process and nowhere else. | Rust test `a_real_native_plugin_loads_in_the_child_and_only_there` — `crates/plugin-host/tests/process_backend.rs` |
| A tool call reaches the registration the plugin installed in the host process. | Rust test `a_real_tool_call_reaches_a_registration_inside_the_child` — `crates/plugin-host/tests/process_backend.rs` |
| An LLM call reaches the registration the plugin installed in the host process. | Rust test `an_llm_execution_intercept_wraps_a_call_across_the_boundary` — `crates/plugin-host/tests/process_backend.rs` |
| An LLM sanitizer in the child resolves the call's codec through the kernel, in both directions. | Rust test `a_real_llm_request_sanitizer_resolves_the_calls_codec_through_the_kernel` — `crates/plugin-host/tests/process_backend.rs`<br>Rust test `a_real_llm_response_sanitizer_resolves_the_calls_codec_through_the_kernel` — `crates/plugin-host/tests/process_backend.rs` |
| A plugin that registers every class is served whole, and its registration set is inspected over the boundary rather than loaded here. | Rust test `the_full_fixture_is_served_whole_by_the_boundary` — `crates/plugin-host/tests/process_backend.rs`<br>Rust test `the_full_fixture_is_inspectable_over_the_boundary` — `crates/plugin-host/tests/process_backend.rs` |

| A host built from another release is refused before any operation is sent to it. | Rust test `a_host_from_another_release_is_refused_before_any_operation` — `crates/plugin-host/tests/process_backend.rs` |
| An answer that outgrows its operation is refused by the kernel rather than accepted as the operation's result. | Rust test `an_answer_that_outgrows_its_operation_is_refused_by_the_kernel` — `crates/plugin-host/tests/process_backend.rs` |
| The host process runs under the limits it was started with, and the default profile bounds what one plugin can take. | Rust test `the_host_runs_under_the_limits_it_was_started_with` — `crates/plugin-host/tests/process_backend.rs`<br>Rust test `the_default_profile_bounds_what_one_plugin_can_take` — `crates/plugin-host/src/limits.rs` |

## Asserted, not yet enforced

Claims the milestone makes that no test covers. They are listed rather than
left out, because a gap that is written down is one somebody can close.

| claim | why it is not enforced |
|---|---|
| The CLI's server starts plugins in the host process. | The CLI composes the shared activation in `crates/cli/src/server/mod.rs`, so it is the same path the shared tests drive and the same composition the architecture check keeps singular. What is missing is a CLI test that asserts the boundary from the CLI: its own suite covers plugin lifecycle, snapshots and trust, and none of those would notice if the server went back to loading in process. |
| Every consumer that hosts plugins resolves the host from the package that shipped it rather than from a search. | Python resolves the host its wheel carries from the installed package, and Node resolves the platform package's `bin/`; both are checked by their verifiers. The FFI and the CLI have no packaging step of their own yet, so there is nothing to resolve and nothing to check. |
